title: Mode 1 'Choose up to 3 cards from opponents' trashes. Their owners recycle them.' recycles the CASTER's own trash instead of opponents' and gives no target prompt.
expected: Card def (riftbound-cards/src/cards/unl/disposal-order.ts:24-34) emits {type:'recycle', amount:3, from:'trash', target:{controller:'enemy', location:'trash', quantity:{upTo:3}, type:'card'}} with no `owner` or top-level `upTo`. In handle_recycle (riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/recycle.ts:129-166) the counted `from:'trash'` branch builds `owners = effect.owner==='any' ? allPlayers : [ctx.playerId]` (lines 134-137) and pools only those trashes (138-140) — never consulting effect.target.controller, so it pools the CASTER's trash. `upTo` is read from `effect.upTo === true` (line 145), not target.quantity.upTo, so upTo=false; with n = min(3, pool.length) == pool.length the prompt branch (149) is skipped and lines 162-165 auto-recycle every card in the caster's trash. Matches observed: no prompt, p1's own trash (1 or 2 Disposal Orders) recycled to p1 deck, p2 trash untouched.
observed: No prompt appeared. Player-2's trash stayed at 4 cards / deck 33. Instead every card in player-1's trash (first run: the just-resolved Disposal Order itself, p1 deck 33->34; second run: two Disposal Orders, p1 trash 2->0, deck 32->34) was auto-recycled to the bottom of player-1's deck. Root cause in engine handle_recycle (abilities/effects/recycle.ts): the counted 'from: trash' branch pools only ctx.playerId's trash unless effect.owner==='any' and reads effect.upTo, ignoring the card's target {controller:'enemy', location:'trash', quantity:{upTo:3}} — so the enemy filter and the up-to/optional prompt are both dropped.

history.note: handle_recycle counted branch: scope pool via effect.owner ?? target.controller (enemy/any) and treat target.quantity.upTo as up-to prompt

resolution.note: handle_recycle counted branch: scope pool via effect.owner ?? target.controller (enemy/any) and treat target.quantity.upTo as up-to prompt
